sections.heading: Distinguish filing, effectiveness, renewal and changes
paragraphs: Under section 14-218, absent a stop order, registration automatically takes effect at noon on the 30th business day after the application or last amendment is filed, or at an earlier time set by the Commissioner. A receipt alone therefore does not establish that the registration is effective.

Section 14-219 normally uses the first anniversary and requires renewal materials at least 15 business days before expiration, subject to its order and other conditions. Record the actual effective and expiry dates. Under section 14-220, material changes require a prompt amendment; if approved, its effective date is set by the Commissioner. Do not invent a fixed 30-day amendment period or wait for annual renewal.

These can respectively involve releasing a claim, transferring rights, replacing an obligation or party, giving up rights, or preventing a person from asserting a position. Flag any such effect in the agreement, questionnaire or side paper.

Keep this restriction within its stated scope. It does not by itself decide every later settlement, termination condition or choice-of-law question. Separately, COMAR .09 requires covered franchise advertising for an offering subject to registration to be submitted at least five days before anticipated initial use. Preserve the exact material, sponsor, channel and first-use date.

sections.heading: Ask who provides services to whom
paragraphs: General Laws chapter 149, section 148B begins with an individual performing services. That starting condition must be applied to the actual relationship and relevant current case law. Do not skip directly to the contractor conditions without identifying the service and the possible employer.

A brand owner, local operator company, individual owner-manager, employed supervisor and field technician have different roles. One person’s classification does not automatically establish everyone else’s. Nor does managerial independence at the overseas parent settle how people doing the U.S. work should be treated.

sections.heading: All three stated conditions matter
paragraphs: The statutory independent-contractor exception requires all three conditions: freedom from control and direction both in the contract and in fact; service outside the employer’s usual course of business; and an independently established business of the same nature as the service performed.

These are cumulative conditions. Evidence of independence on one point does not remove the other two. For example, letting someone choose a work schedule would not by itself show that the service is outside the alleged employer’s usual business or that the person runs an independently established business. The legal application still depends on the services threshold, actual facts and relevant cases.

sections.heading: Compare written responsibilities with daily practice
paragraphs: Collect the agreement, but also record who actually sets schedules, prices work, recruits people, supplies tools, supervises performance and pays the individual. A contract can say the operator is independent while the working arrangements need a closer examination.

Describe which entity holds the customer contract, issues the invoice and receives payment. Those details help the reviewer distinguish a local company’s commercial relationship with the brand from an individual’s service relationship with a possible employer. A franchise label neither makes every franchisee an employee nor establishes contractor status.

List the operating requirements, use of the brand and required payment flows. Then investigate actual fee exclusions and other scope questions separately. A licence heading or a federal classification answer does not automatically decide the Michigan result. The full current section 445.1502 and section 445.1527 routes were blocked in the recorded review, so a complete exceptions or ongoing-contract analysis is not claimed.

sections.heading: Apply Minnesota’s own definition
paragraphs: Current section 80C.01, subdivision 4 includes a route involving brand rights, a community of interest and a direct or indirect fee. It also contains other branches concerning fuel, specified business-opportunity promises and certain security-system payments. The federal control-or-assistance test is not a substitute for this state wording.

Prepare a factsheet of the rights, brand use, shared marketing interest, goods, services, training and required initial or recurring payments. Examine area-franchise scope, fee definitions, exclusions and any claimed wholesale or fair-market-value payment treatment separately. This review identifies the questions; it does not determine that the actual arrangement is covered or exempt.

sections.heading: Use the effective registration order
paragraphs: Section 80C.02 requires an effective registration before a covered offer or sale unless the franchise or transaction is exempt under section 80C.03. The Department directs electronic filings through ComOnline. A prepared application is not the same as an effective registration.

Under section 80C.08, the registration is effective for 12 months from the Commissioner’s order, and the prescribed annual report must be filed before that period ends. Retain the order and actual end date. Renewing a registration is a different matter from renewing an existing operator’s contract.

sections.heading: Check when initial fees can actually be used
paragraphs: The financial-assurance guidance says the Commissioner may require escrow, impoundment or deferral where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated. It describes a surety-bond alternative and deferral of initial franchise fees until the franchisee has opened.

These are possible conditions in the actual review, not restrictions automatically imposed on every applicant. Read the selected condition and release requirements. Money expected at signature may not be available when the seller needs to pay trainers or travel costs. Recording fee revenue in accounts does not establish spendable cash.

The finance director lists the payment dates and identifies committed capital available during the gap. If a different assurance applies, the calculation must use its actual terms instead. For a franchise subject to state registration requirements, provide the current public offering statement and all proposed agreements at least seven days before the earlier of execution of any franchise or other agreement or payment of consideration. Consideration means the relevant payment or other value.

Obtain a signed acknowledgement before agreement or payment and retain it for three years from taking it. The independent federal 14-calendar-day disclosure requirement remains applicable where its coverage requires it. Seven state-law days do not shorten that federal period. Keep the documents, triggers, delivery and acknowledgement dates separately.

sections.heading: Keep existing-operator decisions separate
paragraphs: The separate Minnesota relationship guide addresses section 80C.14’s termination, nonrenewal and transfer branches. A valid annual registration does not itself approve ending a contract, refusing to renew it or rejecting a transfer.

The company secretary and finance director should finish this sales plan together: registration order and annual report dates; buyer documents and receipt retention; initial support costs; available committed funds; and the selected assurance and release evidence. Any exemption or financial condition must be tied to the actual transaction and order.

seoTitle: Minnesota Franchise Termination, Nonrenewal and Transfers

sections.heading: Define the covered relationship and actual action
paragraphs: Start with section 80C.01’s franchise definition and the recognized-classification context in section 80C.14, subdivisions 1–2. Do not assume one rule applies to every commercial or sector arrangement. Then describe whether management proposes termination or cancellation, failure to renew, or withholding consent to a transfer.

Registration expiry and contract expiry are separate events. A filing calendar does not decide whether ending the operator’s agreement is lawful. Keep the contract term, actual conduct and intended result in the decision file.

sections.heading: For termination, examine cause and notice separately
paragraphs: Subdivision 3 requires good cause. It states a 90-day written notice containing all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct the failure, subject to separate immediate-effect exceptions. Preserve whether the requirement was material and reasonable, what failed, the reasons stated, actual receipt and the correction history.

The immediate-effect exceptions concern specified abandonment, a business-related conviction and the prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch. A fact listed as good cause does not automatically appear in the immediate-notice exception list. The goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice. A clause allowing immediate termination for breach does not establish those statutory facts.

sections.heading: For nonrenewal, use the separate statutory branches
paragraphs: Subdivision 4 separately addresses good-cause and failure-to-correct cases. It also has a route requiring at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from the failure to renew.

Do not translate that language into an automatic cash refund, a guaranteed compensation payment or repayment of the initial fee. It requires examination of the statutory operating opportunity and value. The provision also prohibits refusing renewal for the purpose of converting the franchisee’s premises to the franchisor’s own operation. Record the real business plan, not merely the letter’s chosen heading.

sections.heading: For transfer, compare the proposed buyer with current standards
paragraphs: Subdivision 5 addresses unreasonably withholding consent where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Collect those current standards and the proposed buyer’s evidence, then record the actual reasons for the decision.

This is not a rule requiring approval of every transfer. Nor should an unsupported statement that a buyer is unsuitable replace comparison with the present qualifications and standards. The practical task is a documented decision on the actual proposed replacement.

paragraphs: For the weak-performance example, separate the purpose, claimed failure and notice/cure history. Going-concern valuation and actual legal outcomes remain undecided.

sections.heading: Start with the business using the software
paragraphs: Imagine a manufacturer asking its Montana partner to connect its customer-management system to a new supplier portal. The system may contain warranty records, customer contacts and sales information. Signing a general brand agreement does not answer who may receive each part of that information.

Montana section 30-11-717 uses a particular meaning of dealer, linked to the new motor vehicle dealer definition in 61-4-201. An ordinary service franchise, standalone repair shop or used-only dealer has not been shown to qualify simply because it uses dealer software. The first document to prepare is a short explanation of which legal business fits which definition.

sections.heading: Permission needs its own document
paragraphs: For covered third-party access, the prescribed permission must be prior, express and written, in a document separate from other consent, contract or franchise writings. It must identify the sharing parties and contain the required details about what sharing is allowed and for how long. A broad paragraph inside the software subscription is not a substitute for checking those requirements.

Section 718 also restricts access, use, sharing and specified interference through technology or contracts, and addresses cyber ransom. List the actual manufacturer, software vendor, authorised integrator and other recipients: their legal roles can produce different duties.

sections.heading: Withdrawing access and ending a contract use different clocks
paragraphs: Under section 718, the prescribed consent can be revoked or amended on 30 days’ notice without cause, and immediately for cause. Sections 719–720 separately address vendor or integrator contract termination on their stated 90-day terms. These are different decisions; a long subscription term does not settle whether particular data permission continues.

The transition provisions also concern usable electronic data, return or deletion following the dealer’s written directions, recipient lists and audit access. An audit is a check of what happened to the data. Plan the successor’s access, export format and lawful retention before the old connection is switched off.

sections.heading: Why the campaign needs a legal decision first
paragraphs: A brand may prepare a website, book a Nebraska recruitment advertisement and arrange calls with prospective operators before anyone signs a contract. Nebraska’s relevant filing trigger can arise during that earlier activity. The selling business therefore needs a decision before the campaign, not only a check on signing day.

Section 59-1722 creates a conditional franchise exemption from the SAMP Act. The current statute incorporates specified federal provisions as they existed on January 1, 2026. Establishing the exemption means checking those incorporated conditions; using the word licence or holding a completed FDD does not establish compliance by itself.

sections.heading: What the qualifying franchise route requires
paragraphs: The statute requires notice and a $100 fee before the specified Nebraska-based advertising, offers or representations to Nebraska prospects. Some state prohibitions remain applicable despite the exemption. Describe where the advertisement is placed, who receives the offer and which entity is selling, so the reviewer can apply the actual trigger.

The notice identifies the seller, contact details, operating name and plan description. The regulator describes the qualifying franchise notice as a one-time filing without renewal, while distinguishing contact-only amendments from other changes. Keep that distinction when updating the company record: “one time” is not a reason to ignore every later change. Acknowledgment records a filing event; it does not approve the offering or verify statements about profit.

sections.heading: If the exemption is not established, investigate the other route
paragraphs: A covered nonexempt SAMP has a different process. Section 59-1724 provides for a prior disclosure filing and $100 fee, material-change filings and annual updates. A material change is a change important to the required information; it cannot simply be parked until the next sales cycle.

Section 59-1732 also addresses disclosure at the first specified in-person or written communication and at least 48 hours before the relevant contract or consideration. Those state rules do not shorten an independently applicable federal disclosure period. First determine which rules cover the transaction, then put each applicable clock on the calendar.

sections.heading: A multiplication is a scenario, not proof
paragraphs: The statute expressly says that multiplying sales by profit per sale is insufficient substantiation. Its required information includes the seller’s selling history, the number and percentage of purchasers forming the representation’s basis, and purchasers known to attain the stated results.

The number and percentage tell the buyer how much of the purchaser population supports the claim. For example, a result drawn from a small selected group cannot be understood without knowing who was included, who was left out and how the results were measured. Keep the underlying records so a reviewer can follow the calculation back to actual experience. This is different from choosing inputs that produce a desirable answer.

sections.heading: A filed sales notice does not decide the relationship question

The statutory definition includes specific nonalcoholic-beverage wording and excludes petroleum arrangements. It also defines franchise fee and good cause. Record the actual rights and payments rather than relying on what the parties call the agreement.

sections.heading: Apply all three statutory criteria
paragraphs: Section 87-403 requires the stated Nebraska place of business, gross sales of covered products or services between the parties exceeding $35,000 in the 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed, and more than 20 percent of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise. The criteria are cumulative: meeting one does not replace the others.

The place-of-business definition concerns a fixed place where the operator displays and sells goods or offers and sells the franchisor’s services. It expressly excludes an office, warehouse, storage place, residence or vehicle. An address in Nebraska is therefore not enough by itself. The sales amounts are tests for this law, not a general minimum business size for entering the state.

sections.heading: Why this is an equipment question
paragraphs: Nevada NRS 597.112–597.118 concerns defined farm-equipment dealer relationships. Its tests include retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial dependence on a supplier. Inventory means the defined farm equipment, attachments or repair parts. A maintenance-service brand or software licence does not fit merely because the parties use the word dealer.

The supplier and proposed operator should list the actual machines, parts, distribution rights and sources of revenue. That list helps the reviewer apply the statutory definition instead of copying a rule from another industry.

sections.heading: Termination and nonrenewal have a particular procedure
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 addresses good cause and generally requires 180 days’ written reasons before termination or nonrenewal, with 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Listed grounds receive different treatment, and market-share failures have an assistance condition. The general periods therefore cannot be applied without checking the reason for action.

A contractual end date does not complete the analysis. Keep the alleged deficiency, performance evidence, support offered and proposed corrective steps together. They help explain whether the applicable statutory branch has been followed; simply waiting out a notice period cannot establish good cause.

sections.heading: A major amendment is not automatically governed by the same clock
paragraphs: Section 597.1143(1) also requires good cause for a substantial change of a covered agreement’s terms. Section 597.115(4) addresses termination, nonrenewal and those changes because of natural disaster, labour dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver or modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

The 180-day notice and 60-day correction provisions in subsections (2)–(3) concern termination and nonrenewal. They do not establish a universal 180-day notice for every amendment. Compare the old and proposed terms and explain why the supplier wants the change.

paragraphs: Fictional example: a European manufacturer appoints a Nevada dealer to sell agricultural machines, stock parts and perform branded servicing. Later, the manufacturer considers changing the agreement substantially or ending it after weak sales. The manager first checks whether the arrangement falls within the farm-equipment definitions.

The team then separates the proposed action from its reason. A substantial amendment raises the good-cause question; a termination or nonrenewal also requires the correct notice and correction analysis. If the problem is market share, the assistance condition needs attention. If a natural disaster affected performance, the separate uncontrollable-circumstances provision must be examined. The same notice template cannot answer every branch.

sections.heading: Start with the actual offer, not its name
paragraphs: A supplier might call its partner a master franchisee, regional licensee or representative. The test concerns participants who make an investment and receive rights to recruit others for economic gain, with those further participants also investing and receiving recruiting rights. paragraphs: The law expressly says that limiting the number of participants or adding eligibility conditions does not itself change the identity of the defined scheme. A cap can affect the commercial scale without resolving the statutory structure.

Where the prohibited device is established, the chapter prohibits promotion, offering or granting participation. The company therefore needs the review before recruitment activity, rather than waiting to see whether the network becomes large or profitable. This page does not conclude that every multi-level business or master franchise is unlawful.

sections.heading: New York’s definition has alternative branches
paragraphs: The Attorney General says covered offerings must be registered before franchises are offered or sold in or from New York unless an exemption applies. General Business Law (GBL) 681(3) has two alternative franchise branches: a substantially prescribed marketing plan plus a required direct or indirect fee, or substantial association with the designated commercial symbol plus that fee. Both the plan and symbol elements are not required in every arrangement.

Section 681 also addresses fee exclusions, area/subfranchise roles, uninterrupted renewals and state connections. Part 200.1 adds fee and advice/training meanings. List the actual seller, rights, payments, support, offers, acceptances and operating locations before applying a branch or exemption. This guide does not classify a particular transaction.

sections.heading: Disclosure can be due before the expected signing date
paragraphs: GBL 683(8) requires the offering prospectus—the seller’s required disclosure information—and proposed agreements at the earliest of the first personal meeting, at least ten business days before a binding franchise or other agreement, or at least ten days before receipt of consideration. It defines the covered first face-to-face meeting by its purpose of discussing a sale or possible franchise sale. Record the meeting’s purpose as well as its date.

The currently linked Attorney General addendum, revised April 2, 2024, instead uses ten-business-day wording alongside execution or related payment. Preserve that literal source difference. The federal 14-calendar-day requirement is independent: it does not justify ignoring the state’s earlier meeting or payment trigger. Do not silently change the statute’s ten-day payment language into ten business days.

sections.heading: Annual renewal follows the accounting calendar
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s guide directs annual renewal submissions within 120 days after the franchisor’s fiscal year end. It distinguishes a timely pending renewal from expired registration. If registration expires, the guide says there can be no covered offers or sales within or from New York until renewal is submitted and accepted for filing.

The renewal package includes an updated FDD, marked changes, accountant consent, franchise-sales information, prices, credit terms and audited financial statements. Finance and sales teams must both contribute. An internal preparation schedule is a useful business control; it does not change the legal deadline.

sections.heading: New information and new advertising need their own checks
paragraphs: Part 200.5 requires prompt notification by an application to amend for material prospectus changes. Its examples include fees, specified significant adverse business/obligation/agreement/product or model changes and stated financial information. Keep a change register independently of the annual renewal.

The agency guide also calls for two copies of franchise advertising through FRED at least seven days before intended use. FRED is the franchise filing system of the North American Securities Administrators Association (NASAA). Annual renewal does not complete that separate campaign task; current guidance controls the submission channel.

paragraphs: Section 51-19-02 covers the stated combination of marketing plan/system, commercial symbol and direct or indirect fee, including area-franchise scope. Required goods or services can matter. Its wholesale-goods exclusion has a reasonable-quantity condition, so purchasing stock is not automatically outside the fee inquiry.

The section also defines state-connected offers/acceptances and distinguishes uninterrupted renewals/extensions within its offer/sale definition. That contract-renewal distinction does not cancel the separate duty to renew registration. Identify the parties, payments, location facts and transaction type before selecting an exemption.

sections.heading: Submission and effectiveness are different events
paragraphs: Section 51-19-03 requires registration or an applicable exemption before a covered offer or sale. Under 51-19-07, filing, entry into the register by the Commissioner—the responsible state official—and the absence of a stop order matter to effectiveness. A submitted application is not itself proof that every condition has been met.

Material changes require prompt written amendment notification; approved amendments take effect on the Commissioner’s date. Any conditional fee escrow/impoundment or surety alternative also depends on the statute and actual order. Keep these conditions with the offering’s cash and date records.

sections.heading: Renewal comes before the expiry-day reminder
paragraphs: The agency directs renewal no later than fifteen business days before registration expires unless the Commissioner waives the period. It describes a twelve-month registration period unless an order or rule says otherwise. Use the effective and expiry dates from the actual registration record.

The agency also says that from April 1, 2026 a state-specific FDD addendum is no longer required. This changes one document task. It does not remove registration, financial review, disclosure or amendment responsibilities.

sections.heading: Update only the checklist item the notice actually changed
paragraphs: The change is one document task, not a finding that financial review, amendments or other requirements disappeared.

The renewal owner still checks the FDD, marked changes, accountant consent, seller forms and advertising not previously filed. Finance examines any financial-assurance condition. The owner records the fifteen-business-day deadline and any actual waiver rather than relying on a reminder sent on expiry day. The narrow change saves the wrong document from being prepared; it does not make the whole renewal unnecessary.

paragraphs: Section 51-19-08(6) has its stated seven-day prospectus/agreement delivery rule before the earlier agreement or consideration, plus a signed receipt and three-year receipt retention. The independently applicable federal 14-calendar-day rule is not shortened by that state text.

Section 51-19-16(7) separately makes purported waiver of compliance with the chapter, rules or orders void. This is the named anti-waiver provision, not a complete answer about every termination, renewal or industry protection. The agency’s broad count of registration states is also not used here as a national classification.

seoTitle: Ohio Business Opportunities: Exemption Duties That Remain

sections.heading: An exemption can preserve named duties
paragraphs: Section 1334.13 exempts materially FTC-compliant transactions from most of Ohio’s Business Opportunity Plans chapter. Its opening wording preserves sections 1334.03(H) and 1334.04. Those provisions address representations that a payment or note is secured, or that a buyback arrangement exists, and related bond or trust requirements.

The practical question is therefore not just “Did we provide an FDD?” An FDD is information for a prospective franchise buyer. The company must retain evidence of the relevant federal compliance and examine any preserved Ohio provision triggered by the actual promises.

sections.heading: Start with Ohio’s own definitions and proof requirements
paragraphs: Section 1334.01 defines the state arrangement using supplied goods or services, payment conditions and specified representations. Its payment analysis is separate from the federal minimum-payment exemption. Do not substitute a federal payment test for the state definition.

Section 1334.12 contains other exceptions. In cases under sections 1334.08 or 1334.09, section 1334.14 places proof of an exemption or exception on the person claiming it. A written explanation linked to the facts is therefore more useful than an unexplained box marked exempt.

sections.heading: Two self-checks for the secured-equipment promise
paragraphs: The European seller’s FDD and marketing reassurance answer different questions. Neither is a universal exemption result.

paragraphs: Fictional example: a European technical-services brand gives an Ohio prospect an FDD. Its salesperson also says the startup payment is “fully secured” because the brand will buy back equipment if the unit closes. Those words create a separate question from whether the federal disclosure process was completed.

The finance manager keeps the precise statement, identifies who made it and obtains the actual buyback agreement. The reviewer checks the surviving Ohio security/buyback provisions and any bond or trust requirement, including the required amount if applicable. A verbal reassurance or an accounting entry is not a substitute for analysing the promised protection.

The example does not establish that this offer is covered or that a particular financial arrangement satisfies the law. It shows why marketing language and the finance documents need to be reviewed together.

sections.heading: The nonexempt route has its own buyer protections
paragraphs: For a covered plan without an established exemption, the chapter has disclosure, claim-substantiation, contract and cancellation provisions. The basic disclosure period is ten business days before agreement. Ohio’s reviewed definition excludes Sunday and legal holidays; a standard Monday–Friday calculator may produce the wrong count.

Cancellation under section 1334.05 is a separate conditional process, not a universal right for every franchise buyer to cancel. Determine the applicable route and conditions before describing any cancellation right or preparing the contract notice. Independently applicable federal requirements remain separate.

Assign finance to the bond/trust question and any required amount or supporting document.
For a covered nonexempt plan, build the correct business-day calendar and contract/cancellation record.

seoTitle: Oklahoma Business Opportunities: Exemption and Filing

sections.heading: Identify exactly what the disclosure exemption removes
paragraphs: The Oklahoma Business Opportunity Sales Act prohibits covered offers or sales without registration or an exemption. Section 803(6) provides a disclosure-based exemption for specified business opportunities or franchises when the stated document is delivered 14 calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration.

The provision exempts sections 806–811 rather than the whole Act. Record the exact paragraph being used, which duties it removes and what remains. Merely preparing a document does not establish delivery, recipient or timing.

sections.heading: Use the state definition and actual locations
paragraphs: Section 802 contains Oklahoma definitions of business opportunity, franchise and marketing plan. Promises about finding accounts and providing training can be relevant. A separate registered-mark/net-worth exclusion has further conditions; a registered mark alone does not establish it.

Section 805 places the burden of proving an exemption, exclusion or exception on its claimant. Section 818 separately examines the relevant offer origin and receipt, acceptance, domicile and operating-location facts. Domicile concerns the legally relevant home connection, rather than just where a salesperson happens to be travelling. An internet campaign needs its actual communications analysed; this guide supplies no blanket rule for discovery calls.

sections.heading: Do not use one completed document to close all three routes
paragraphs: The advertising question remains independently assigned. No new procedure or exemption is supplied here.

paragraphs: Section 807 describes a complete filing, effectiveness normally after 15 full business days absent the stated orders or proceedings, and a one-year duration. Keep completeness, submission, applicable orders and effectiveness evidence together. The period is not an unconditional promise that any incomplete upload becomes effective.

Sections 819–822 address fraud and misleading claims, including presenting a filing as approval. The current administrative advertising-filing rule could not be confirmed because the agency site failed. That is an unresolved task, not evidence that advertising has no requirements.

seoTitle: Oregon Franchise Disclosure Without Filing Approval

sections.heading: Understand the narrow filing answer
paragraphs: DFR says Oregon does not require franchisors to file franchise documents and obtain approval before a franchise sale. The same agency page requires disclosure at least 14 days before signing a contract or paying money. “No filing approval” describes that process; it does not establish that the offering is outside state law.

The agency identifies ORS Chapter 650 and OAR Chapter 441 Division 325, complaint handling and a private civil remedy. A private remedy means an affected person may have the stated court-based route; this page does not decide whether a particular claim succeeds.

sections.heading: Establish the actual agreement and geographic facts
paragraphs: The reviewed 2025 official text of ORS 650.005 describes the marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration franchise test. It defines a franchisor as a person, including a subfranchisor, who sells a franchise for $100 or more to a franchisee or subfranchisor. The $100 wording is part of that stated seller definition, not a conclusion about all low-fee arrangements.

Section 650.015 separately addresses offer origin/direction, acceptance and the stated domicile/operation facts. Record these connections before applying the law. An outlet address alone does not answer all the questions, and other business-model or sector rules remain separate.

sections.heading: Give the buyer the complete proposed package in time
paragraphs: OAR 441-325-0020 requires the disclosure document and all proposed sale agreements at least 14 calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration event, including refundable deposits. An agreement draft and a deposit can matter before the formal opening date.

The current rules distinguish exceptions for unchanged renewals, added units and owner resales. Those branches need their own facts and change records; an existing relationship alone does not establish an exception. The separate Oregon renewal/additional-unit guide explains those distinctions.

paragraphs: Correcting the worksheet is a preparation step, not a classification or permission to sell.

Finance keeps the transaction’s proceeds traceable. Customer procurement, employment and tax questions are separate tasks; none is settled by the franchise filing answer. This is a fictional planning sequence, not a classification or permission to sell.

paragraphs: DFR identifies complete books, records and franchise-sale details, including distribution of proceeds. A useful file shows which documents were sent, to whom and when, what was signed and what money was received. seoTitle: Oregon Franchise Renewals, Additional Units and Resales

sections.heading: Use Oregon’s definitions before choosing an exception
paragraphs: ORS 650.005 permits oral or written arrangements within its stated marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration franchise test. A franchisor is a person, including a subfranchisor, selling a franchise for $100 or more to a franchisee or subfranchisor.

The statute’s sale definition separately excludes the stated unchanged uninterrupted renewal/extension. This is not a conclusion that every low-fee or amended arrangement is exempt. The federal rules and other state branches have independent tests. Describe the actual rights, payments and proposed change first.

sections.heading: A continuing relationship needs three checks
paragraphs: OAR 441-325-0030(2) addresses renewal, extension, amendment or modification only where there is no interruption in operation of the relationship, no material change adverse to the franchisee in the relationship, and no material change adverse to the franchisee in previously supplied disclosure information.

These are three conditions, not interchangeable descriptions of a familiar buyer. Compare both the agreement and the earlier disclosure with what is now proposed. An unchanged cover page cannot prove that support charges, rights or disclosed information have stayed unchanged.

sections.heading: Another franchise has a different information test
paragraphs: The additional-unit branch in 0030(3) requires prior disclosure in connection with the earlier sale and no material adverse change in the disclosure information supplied. Keep the earlier disclosure and receipt, but also investigate subsequent changes. Do not simply copy the renewal checklist.

If no exception is established, 0020 requires the disclosure and all proposed sale agreements at least 14 calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration, including refundable deposits. A refundable payment is not automatically outside that clock.

sections.heading: Choose the Oregon transaction before using an exception
paragraphs: In the revised-support-charge example, classify the added franchise and compare old/new information before deciding whether an exception is established. Otherwise retain the ordinary delivery task.

paragraphs: Fictional example: an Irish IT-services brand offers its existing Oregon operator a second territory. At the same time, the brand revises support charges and financial disclosures. The sales manager initially calls the transaction a renewal because the operator already belongs to the network.

The manager instead identifies the additional franchise and retrieves the earlier disclosure. A change log compares the fees and financial information with the documents the operator previously received. The reviewer applies the additional-unit conditions to the actual changes. If the conditions cannot be established, the ordinary complete-package delivery task stays open and the deposit schedule is adjusted for review.
This example does not decide that the changes are materially adverse. It shows the evidence needed before relying on that conclusion, rather than letting a sales label make the decision.

sections.heading: A resale is another distinct branch
paragraphs: The franchisee-own-account route in 0030(4) includes no-franchisor-involvement, isolated-sale and specified 14-day full-record-access conditions. Rule 0040 separately describes a chapter exemption for the stated own-account/entire-area resale without franchisor participation or aid.

The rules address approval rights alone, but active marketing or assistance can change the facts. Record exactly what the franchisor does. This guide does not reconcile every possible overlap between these resale provisions or approve a transfer.

seoTitle: Pennsylvania Vehicle-Dealer Inventory Repurchase Timing

sections.heading: Check the business and the property first
paragraphs: The Board of Vehicles Act has defined vehicle-dealer and franchise coverage. Section 316 concerns eligible inventory and equipment after specified termination or nonrenewal events. A cleaning or IT brand cannot use these numbers as a general service-franchise exit formula.

Even for a relevant dealer, the accounting category “stock” is too broad to decide eligibility. Product category, condition, acquisition age and other statutory limits matter. Motorcycle, recreational-vehicle and manufactured-housing arrangements need particular attention to their treatment under the section.

sections.heading: There are two events and two clocks
paragraphs: Section 316 generally requires covered property to be returned within 90 days of the relevant termination or nonrenewal. It separately requires repurchase/payment within 60 days of tender. The starting events differ: a relationship’s effective end date is not automatically the date property was tendered.

The company should obtain return instructions and retain the evidence of tender and actual return. Neither an invoice total nor an assumption that the 90 days have passed establishes when the payment clock began. Apply the precise statutory event and eligibility requirements before calculating any claimed due date.

sections.heading: Two starting events, not one exit countdown
paragraphs: This is the defined vehicle-dealer section 316 process, not a formula refunding every service-franchise investment.

paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign vehicle manufacturer appoints a Pennsylvania franchised dealer. The dealer acquires vehicles, spare parts, required tools and branded signs. Years later, the parties face an exit. Finance’s first report shows one overall inventory value, but that number cannot establish what qualifies for repurchase.

The team separates each category. Vehicle rows show serial numbers, acquisition dates, mileage and condition. Parts rows include the relevant catalogue records. Tools and signs have their own purchase and requirement evidence. Any secured creditor is identified rather than being overlooked in a general stock total.

The operations manager then links the inventory file to the effective termination/nonrenewal event and to the return instructions, tender evidence and return record. Finance can now ask which items qualify, what valuation or condition questions remain and when the relevant payment period starts. The example organises the evidence; it does not decide eligibility or guarantee reimbursement.

sections.heading: Keep commercial planning distinct from legal entitlement
paragraphs: Keeping these records from the start is a business planning choice that makes a later review possible. It does not enlarge the statutory categories. A dealer may have spent money that is commercially important but does not fall within the relevant repurchase provision.

The same distinction matters when pricing a new relationship. Budgeting for inventory, tools and financing is sensible, but management should not assume that every amount is recoverable at exit. Use the actual statutory category and conditions rather than describing section 316 as an automatic refund of the investment.

seoTitle: Rhode Island Franchise Filing Periods and Renewals

sections.heading: Define the relationship and the state connections
paragraphs: Section 19-28.1-3 uses a marketing-plan/brand/fee-in-excess-of-$500 test and a separate master-franchise alternative. Its wholesale exclusion concerns reasonable quantities of tangible goods. These are state tests; do not replace the stated amount or conditions with a different federal exemption.

Section 4 separately examines offer and acceptance connections, including an outside-state sale to a resident where the franchise will operate in Rhode Island. Outlet location alone does not exhaust the inquiry. Record where communications originate and arrive, who accepts and the actual residence/operation facts.

sections.heading: Registration and an exemption notice have different anniversaries
paragraphs: Section 19-28.1-5 prohibits covered offers or sales without registration or exemption. Active rule 230-RICR-50-10-1.4 gives registration a 365-calendar-day period from its initial effective date. It gives an exemption a 365-day period from receipt of the notice. Preserve those actual events in separate calendar fields.

Section 9(d) contains a fiscal-year-based expiry default unless the director prescribes another period by rule or order. The active rule supplies the periods above. The statute also calls for renewal filing 30 days before expiration. Do not choose the statutory default while ignoring the active rule that changes the applicable period.

sections.heading: An exemption from registration is not automatically an exemption from delivery
paragraphs: Section 8 requires disclosure reflecting all material changes and all proposed agreements at least 14 calendar days before execution or payment, subject to its listed exemption subsections. Identify the authority for relief from that requirement separately.

Active rule 1.5 describes a qualified fractional route exempting registration and delivery, with state-specific filing language. Its multiple conditions concern existing experience, location, similarity, expected revenue share and control. A federal fractional exemption does not establish the state route. Section 11 separately requires prompt material-change amendments; the next annual date is not permission to wait after a material event.

sections.heading: A mark is one fact, not the complete answer
paragraphs: Section 39-57-20 covers specified business-startup arrangements and representations. The registered-mark exception appears within its sales/marketing-programme limb. Assistance placing vending machines or similar devices, purchases of products made by the buyer, and guarantee/refund promises have their own terms.

Examine each actual promise together with the fee condition and other exclusions. A brand registration cannot automatically answer an independent guarantee or refund branch. Equally, ordinary help finding customers should not be casually renamed vending-device placement; record what is actually promised.

sections.heading: Filing comes before the covered promotion
paragraphs: For a covered business opportunity, section 39-57-50 requires filing before advertisements or other representations. It requires material-change updates and updates at least biennially, and prescribes use of the assigned registration number in promotion.

Keep the filing receipt and assigned number with the campaign record. A registration number identifies the relevant filing; it is not a government endorsement of the business. Statements about state compliance have separate limits.

The reviewer examines each definition branch and its conditions. Finance investigates the related guarantee, bond/trust and funding questions before sales staff describe the package to prospects.

If the plan is covered, the campaign owner links the proposed material to the filing, assigned number and any required updates. A refund promise is not treated as harmless simply because it sounds reassuring to a buyer. This example demonstrates preparation; it does not decide coverage or the adequacy of financial protection.

paragraphs: Under section 39-57-60(1), earnings claims require documented substantiation disclosed when the representation is made. A management spreadsheet or a sales officer’s confidence is not the same as the required evidence and disclosure. Keep the exact claim and its supporting records together.

Section 39-57-30 separately states a 48-hour disclosure period before the earlier business-opportunity contract or consideration. An independently applicable federal Franchise Rule period remains separate and is not shortened by the state period. This educational article is not the formal disclosure document.
