seoTitle: South Dakota franchise notice: filing, delivery and financial events

sections.heading: Keep a complete filing and its actual receipt
paragraphs: South Dakota Codified Laws (SDCL) 37-5B-4 prohibits a covered offer or sale unless properly notice filed or exempt. Section 5 describes a complete package containing the FDD, application, consent to service and $250 initial fee. It generally becomes effective on receipt, subject to completeness and the stated order/injunction provisions.

A mailing date is not a receipt. Keep the actual evidence and any order affecting the offering. The statute generally provides one year from receipt unless another period is prescribed; it lists a $150 renewal fee and treats late filings as initial filings.

sections.heading: Buyer delivery has more than one condition
paragraphs: Sections 17–18 have an independent 14-calendar-day initial delivery rule and a seven-day branch for unilateral material agreement changes, subject to the actual exemptions. The prospect-initiated-negotiation language in 17(2) does not erase section 26(7)’s separate rule for materially different signing terms. Review both before choosing the execution date.

Section 18 distinguishes delivery/access instructions from first-class mailing: mailing must occur at least three days before the required delivery date. Section 11 requires a prospect-signed receipt before agreement or payment and seller retention for three years. Record the delivery method and actual document version rather than assuming that posting a package is immediate delivery.

sections.heading: No ordinary update filing does not mean no document updating
paragraphs: Section 7 says disclosure updating needs no division filing, while requiring a revised annual document within 120 days of fiscal close and reasonable-time quarterly material-change revisions. Prospects receive the most recent available quarterly revisions. Known financial-performance changes have a separate notice duty.

Section 6 director-required amendments, annual notice renewal and financial-event reporting are independent. The statute requires notice within fifteen days after an auditor reaches the specified going-concern conclusion after effectiveness. An annual expiry reminder will not reliably identify that event.

sections.heading: Sort each date by the event that starts it
paragraphs: In the audit-during-recruitment example, finance owns the auditor-event date, document control owns current disclosure versions, and sales owns delivery and signing evidence. An annual renewal reminder cannot do all three jobs.

headers: Clock or record in the cited provisions
rows: The division receives a complete notice package
SDCL 37-5B-4–5: generally effective on receipt, subject to completeness and the stated order/injunction provisions; the package includes the $250 initial fee.
Mailing is not receipt. The general one-year period can be replaced by another prescribed period; the statute lists $150 renewal and treats late filings as initial filings.
The buyer receives the initial disclosure
Sections 17–18: an independent 14-calendar-day period applies, subject to the actual exemptions.
The stated seven-day unilateral-material-change branch and section 26(7) signing-term rule require separate review; prospect-requested negotiation does not settle both.
The seller uses first-class mailing
Section 18: mailing must occur at least three days before the required delivery date.
Delivery/access instructions are a different branch; posting a package does not automatically establish delivery.
Agreement or payment is approaching
Section 11: obtain the prospect-signed receipt before agreement or payment and retain it for three years.
Keep the document version and delivery evidence with that receipt.
The fiscal year closes or material information changes
Section 7: revise the annual document within 120 days of fiscal close and quarterly material changes within a reasonable time; give prospects the most recent available quarterly revisions.
No ordinary division filing for disclosure updating does not remove document updating, director-required amendments or known financial-performance-change notice.
After effectiveness, the auditor reaches the specified going-concern conclusion
Section 26: notice is due within fifteen days of that conclusion.
This finance event is separate from annual notice renewal and any actual financial-assurance condition.

sections.heading: Worked example: an audit issue during recruitment
paragraphs: Fictional example: a German commercial-cleaning network is recruiting while its finance director receives the auditor’s specified going-concern conclusion. The compliance owner records the conclusion date and the separate fifteen-day task, then examines any actual financial-assurance condition.

Meanwhile, the sales owner checks the current annual document and quarterly revisions before delivering a package. If proposed signing terms change materially, the owner reviews the applicable seven-day and section 26 branches rather than assuming the buyer’s negotiation removes every requirement. The team keeps the signed receipt before agreement or payment.
This example does not determine a particular reporting or exemption outcome. It shows why finance, document control and sales scheduling must communicate during the year.

sections.heading: Advertising still needs truthful support
paragraphs: Section 37-5B-23 says advertisements need not be filed unless the director requests them, while permitting action against misleading advertising. Record the limited filing answer without treating it as permission for unsupported revenue or profit statements.

sections.heading: Keep one calendar with clearly labelled event types
bullets: Retain complete package, actual receipt, effectiveness and any exemption/order evidence.
Assign annual notice renewal separately from annual and quarterly disclosure revisions.
Log initial delivery, mailing allowance, changed agreements and the signed receipt retained for three years.
Assign the auditor-event owner and record the conclusion date promptly.
Keep advertisement versions, claim evidence and any director request.

seoTitle: Tennessee franchise tax versus franchise sales: limits of the FAQs

sections.heading: Two teams may be using the same word differently
paragraphs: The finance director may ask whether the U.S. company needs a Tennessee franchise-tax account. The expansion director may ask whether it can sell branded operating rights. Those questions concern different activities and cannot be answered with one filing receipt.

Tennessee Revenue’s F&E-1 FAQ lists corporations, LLCs and other entity types that may have return obligations. It is a tax resource. The preparer needs the actual taxpayer, entity structure and Tennessee activity before selecting forms; the FAQ does not approve a franchise offering.

sections.heading: Federal treatment does not finish the state tax inquiry
paragraphs: F&E-4 explains that an LLC ignored as a separate entity for federal purposes can still need a Tennessee return unless an exemption applies. Do not translate federal disregarded status into “no state filing”.

The cited agency FAQ pages are dated March 2021. They identify the separation that management must understand, but the preparer still needs current tax-year law, relevant Tennessee connections and exemption conditions before filing. This page does not supply a complete current tax calculation or determine that an exemption applies.

sections.heading: Give the tax preparer and relationship reviewer different facts
paragraphs: The worked example can produce two useful factual handoffs without producing either tax clearance or franchise-sales clearance. The dated sources do not resolve current filing or state franchise-law questions.

rows: Singapore parent, U.S. LLC and Tennessee operator
Identify each entity, its federal tax classification, income and actual Tennessee activities for the relevant tax year.
Identify which entity grants brand rights, receives payments and promises support or control.
The LLC is disregarded for a federal tax purpose
The March 2021 F&E-4 FAQ says that status does not automatically remove a Tennessee return obligation; current law and exemption conditions still need confirmation.
Federal tax classification does not establish the state offer/sale, advertising or relationship rules.
A Tennessee tax account is completed
Retain it as a tax record for the identified taxpayer. It does not supply a complete current tax calculation.
It does not approve recruitment, disclosure, an agreement or termination. Those state-law questions remain unresolved here.
A source cannot be read or is only a consumer-agency explanation
Use the dated FAQs only for the limited entity-versus-tax distinction they establish.
Do not infer an absent franchise duty from failed access or from the June 2021 consumer-agency explanation; keep independently applicable federal disclosure controls.

sections.heading: Worked example: the parent, U.S. LLC and local operator
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore services group forms a U.S. LLC and plans to appoint a Tennessee partner. Finance makes a diagram showing the parent, LLC and operator, which entity earns each type of income and the proposed activities in Tennessee.

The tax preparer uses that factual map to examine current state return and exemption questions, including the relevance of federal classification. Separately, the relationship reviewer receives the actual brand rights, fees, control, support and territory terms. Completing a tax account does not close the early-offer or disclosure tasks.

The sales team keeps independently applicable federal disclosure controls while the unresolved state-law questions are assigned. That is a way to organise the review, not a conclusion that the proposed sale may proceed or that Tennessee has no separate sales obligations.

sections.heading: What the consumer-agency source does not establish
paragraphs: The Attorney General/Division of Consumer Affairs help-centre explanation identifies its consumer-protection role. That article is dated June 2021; it is not current franchise statutory text.

Earlier attempts to read the linked official code and a court document did not yield usable legal text. A page asking for browser verification was rejected rather than treated as law. Consequently, state sales filings, exemptions, advertising and relationship rules remain open questions here. A failed source cannot establish that a duty is absent.

sections.heading: Prepare two clearly separate handoffs
bullets: For the tax preparer, record each entity, federal classification, Tennessee activities and tax year.
Ask the preparer to confirm current state tax scope, exemptions and the filing calendar.
For the relationship reviewer, provide brand, payments, support, control, territory and offer facts.
Assign the unresolved Tennessee offer/sale, advertising and relationship questions explicitly.
Keep applicable federal disclosure controls independent of the tax account.

description: Understand the limited distinction between Tennessee franchise-and-excise tax questions and franchise sales. The 2021 FAQs do not settle current tax or state franchise-law duties.

seoTitle: Texas Form 2703: franchise exemption notice before the offer

sections.heading: The FAQ describes both a condition and a prior filing
paragraphs: Texas Secretary of State FAQ 5 describes the exemption where a franchisor complies in all material respects in Texas with applicable Federal Trade Commission disclosure requirements and prohibitions. The Federal Trade Commission is the U.S. agency responsible for those franchise requirements.

The same FAQ answer requires an exemption notice before offering for sale or selling. Preparing federal disclosure and completing the Texas notice are different events. Retain the evidence supporting compliance and the record of the applicable notice before the covered activity.

sections.heading: Name the business making the offer
paragraphs: Form 2703 asks for the franchisor’s legal name, every name under which it does or intends to do business and its principal business address. The FAQ lists a $25 fee. Identify the actual selling entity rather than automatically inserting the overseas parent because it owns the trademark.

The FAQ describes the notice as one time, without expiry, while saying principal-address changes should be notified in writing. Keep the filed information available to the person monitoring entity and address changes. A no-expiry notice is not an assurance that the underlying offer will always satisfy the exemption conditions.

sections.heading: Fill the Form 2703 decision card before scheduling an offer

headers: Evidence to put in the file
rows: Who is selling the rights?
The actual franchisor legal name, every name under which it does or intends to do business, and its principal business address.
The trademark-owning parent is not automatically the seller; identify the rights seller and relevant payment recipient from the actual arrangement.
Why is the exemption route available?
The Texas offer facts and evidence supporting material compliance in Texas with applicable federal disclosure requirements and prohibitions.
Neither a licence label nor a completed FDD, by itself, establishes the qualifying condition.
What must precede the covered offer or sale?
The applicable Form 2703 notice, the FAQ’s $25 fee, and filing/payment evidence.
Preparing federal disclosure and filing the prior Texas notice are separate events.
What happens after a principal-address change?
Keep the filed record available for the written address-change notification described by the FAQ.
One-time filing without expiry does not guarantee continuing exemption eligibility.
What if the exemption cannot be established?
Keep the nonexempt registration, disclosure and update route open for review.
Do not substitute the one-time notice or a $25 budget for the nonexempt process.

sections.heading: Worked example: a facilities-services campaign
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore facilities brand completes an FDD and plans to recruit Texas partners. Its sales manager marks the filing task unnecessary because the draft agreement calls the operator a licensee.

The company secretary first identifies which legal company will sell the rights and receive the relevant payments. The reviewer examines the actual arrangement, Texas offer facts and the stated federal-compliance condition. If the qualifying route is established, the company prepares and files the applicable notice before the covered offer or sale, retaining the version, payment and filing evidence.

The marketing schedule is linked to that decision instead of treating the contract title or the existence of the FDD as sufficient. If an address later changes, the secretary has the filed record needed to make the written update. This example does not establish that a particular licence is a franchise or that the exemption is available.

sections.heading: The nonexempt route is a different process
paragraphs: The FAQ also describes registration, disclosures and updates for nonexempt business-opportunity sellers. Those are not simply the one-time franchise notice with a different name. If the company cannot establish the exemption conditions, leave the applicable route unresolved and obtain the relevant review rather than budgeting only $25.

Other sales, operating and entity responsibilities remain distinct. The business should record the actual communications and Texas connections for analysis rather than assuming a single phrase about the campaign settles every territorial question.

sections.heading: Keep a clear pre-offer record
bullets: Identify the seller, all operating names and principal business address.
Document the actual relationship, Texas offer facts and the exemption condition.
Retain the Form 2703 version, fee and notice-filing evidence.
Link the planned first covered offer/sale to the completed prior-notice task.
Assign written address-change reporting and keep nonexempt registration, disclosure and other operating questions separate.

title: Texas Form 2703 franchise exemption notice: prepare it before the offer

seoTitle: Texas employee vs independent contractor: unemployment-tax evidence

sections.heading: Name the question being answered
paragraphs: TWC’s guidance concerns the Texas Unemployment Compensation Act. It identifies service, wages and direction or control, and explains that the right to control can be enough even if not exercised. An agreement, trading name or IRS form does not determine the result.

That is why the reviewer needs both the written contract and actual operations. A contract may reserve powers management rarely uses; a short agreement may also fail to describe the detailed instructions given every day. Neither document labels nor assumptions about tax reporting can replace the factual inquiry.

sections.heading: Use the twenty factors as evidence questions
paragraphs: TWC’s comparative guide examines instructions, training, integration into the business, personal service, helpers, continuing relationships, set hours, full-time requirements, work location, sequence, reports, payment, expenses, tools, investment, profit or loss, multiple clients, public availability, discharge and quitting.

Not every factor applies, and its weight can change with the business and facts. This is not a points contest in which eleven favourable answers guarantee a result. Explain what the relevant evidence shows and why, including disputed or mixed facts.

sections.heading: Compare a reserved power with what actually happens
paragraphs: The example raises questions rather than deciding status. A useful memo records both columns, explains mixed facts and identifies which actual document supports each answer.

headers: Actual practice and evidence to examine
rows: Who chooses the method and sequence?
Does the company reserve the power to dictate how the service is performed, even when it rarely intervenes?
The fictional company fixes the route and cleaning sequence. Retain the actual instructions, schedules and communications, not just the contractor label.
Who controls training, tools and help?
Who may require training, choose equipment, hire a helper or allow a substitute?
The fictional company supplies equipment and requires training. Compare that practice with contract clauses and records of who can make those decisions.
Who bears financial risk and serves other customers?
What do payment, expense, investment and termination terms actually allow?
The fictional weekly payment is one fact. Collect invoices, expenses, other-client and public-availability evidence before assessing independence.
Does issuing a 1099 answer the test?
A reporting label does not remove a retained right to control.
No. TWC weighs relevant factors in the Texas unemployment-tax context; there is no eleven-out-of-twenty pass mark and no automatic result for federal tax or wage law.

sections.heading: Worked example: a tightly directed cleaning route
paragraphs: Fictional example: a facilities company describes a worker as a contractor. The company fixes the service route, dictates the cleaning sequence, supplies equipment, requires its training and pays a fixed weekly amount. It plans to issue a 1099 and initially treats that as the end of the question.

The onboarding manager instead collects the contract, route instructions, training records, schedules and payment terms. The reviewer compares retained control rights with actual performance. Who can change the method, hire a helper or substitute someone? Who pays expenses, owns tools and bears the risk of an unprofitable job? Is the worker genuinely available to other customers?

Those facts raise the control issues TWC identifies; the example does not make a final classification. The company records a reasoned Texas unemployment-tax assessment or obtains TWC assistance before relying on the proposed arrangement. Issuing the form cannot cure an unsupported classification.

sections.heading: Turn the assessment into a working record
paragraphs: A useful memo links each relevant fact to an actual source: an invoice, manual, schedule, communication or contract clause. It should explain apparent contradictions instead of selecting only facts that favour the desired classification.

Assign a responsible person to review changes when the worker gains or loses genuine control or financial independence. The review belongs before payroll or contractor onboarding, with later changes documented. A conclusion for this role at this time should not be copied automatically to another state or another type of legal test.

sections.heading: Prepare the role-specific evidence checklist
bullets: Identify the worker, hiring entity, actual role and Texas unemployment-tax question.
Record who controls methods, sequence, hours, attendance and training.
List tools, expenses, helpers/substitutes, investment and potential profit or loss.
Check other clients, public availability, repeated engagements and termination rights.
Attach operational examples and a reasoned assessment; leave federal wage and tax tests separately assigned.

title: Texas employee vs independent contractor: evidence for unemployment tax

seoTitle: Utah franchise notice receipt: issue, renewal and change dates

sections.heading: The trigger includes offers to a Utah resident
paragraphs: Section 13-15-201(2) requires proof of notice receipt before a person offers or sells a franchise to be located in Utah or to a Utah resident. The team must therefore investigate both the proposed operation and the person receiving the offer.

The notice states substantial compliance with the federal Franchise Rule and includes the required applicant, brand, address and identification information. An FDD is the franchise disclosure document prepared for a prospective buyer; preparing it does not itself produce Utah’s receipt.

sections.heading: Use the section effective May 6, 2026
paragraphs: The reviewed current section, amended effective May 6, 2026, makes the receipt valid for one year from issue. Renewal compliance is due at least 30 days before expiry. Filing information that becomes incorrect or incomplete must be updated within 30 days.

These are different dates. Keep the issue date and expiry with the receipt, then record the date information becomes incorrect or incomplete. An annual renewal reminder may arrive too late to catch a change that requires an earlier update.

sections.heading: Build the calendar from four different events
paragraphs: In the campaign example, the issued receipt proves a different event from the address-change record or the FDD delivery record. The secretary and sales owner need all applicable records, not one date labelled filed.

headers: Why another date cannot replace it
rows: The proposed offer reaches the location/resident test
Section 13-15-201(2) requires proof of notice receipt before an offer or sale of a franchise to be located in Utah or to a Utah resident.
An out-of-state outlet does not answer the separate Utah-resident branch; a prepared notice is not issued receipt evidence.
The notice receipt is issued
Under the reviewed section effective May 6, 2026, the receipt is valid for one year from issue. Keep the actual issue and expiry dates.
Do not use an internal drafting or planned-submission date as the start of the issued receipt’s period.
The receipt is approaching expiry
Renewal compliance is due at least 30 days before expiry.
The anniversary is not itself the advance-renewal deadline.
Filed information becomes incorrect or incomplete
Record that event and the separate requirement to update within 30 days.
An address change cannot simply wait for annual renewal.
The buyer must receive documents
Keep independently applicable federal delivery separate; if the qualifying franchise route is unavailable, subsection (1) has its own content and ten-business-day purchaser-disclosure provisions.
A Utah receipt is neither buyer-delivery evidence nor state approval, and the alternative route is not the same notice process.

sections.heading: Worked example: a campaign and an address change
paragraphs: Fictional example: a UK technical-services brand plans a campaign directed to a Utah-resident prospect. While the team prepares the offer, the selling entity changes its principal address. The secretary’s worksheet says the notice was prepared, but the file does not yet contain the issued receipt.

The expansion lead keeps the covered offer subject to the prior-receipt task. The secretary checks the actual selling entity, brand and address information, retains the required receipt and records its issue/expiry dates. The address change is reviewed against the separate 30-day updating requirement rather than waiting until annual renewal.

The sales owner separately records formal FDD delivery and the earliest proposed commitment. This prevents one receipt from being used as evidence of several unrelated events. The example does not determine whether the particular offer qualifies for the notice route or whether any sale may proceed.

sections.heading: If the franchise route is unavailable, the other route is not identical
paragraphs: The Act distinguishes the qualifying franchise notice from the general business-opportunity disclosure filing. Section 201(2)(c) directs those who do not qualify for the notice route to subsection (1), which has its own content and ten-business-day purchaser-disclosure provisions.

Neither receipt is state approval. Any independently applicable federal FDD delivery duty remains a separate task. Identify the actual route and buyer-delivery conditions rather than assuming the simpler notice process applies because the seller uses a franchise label.

sections.heading: Prepare a receipt and change calendar
bullets: Confirm the actual seller, brand names, principal address and required public identifier.
Retain the federal-compliance evidence and issued notice receipt.
Calculate the receipt anniversary and renewal deadline, with an earlier internal preparation date.
Record information changes and the applicable 30-day update task.
Log buyer disclosure and commitments independently; document the alternative route if the notice conditions are not met.

seoTitle: Vermont equipment-dealer termination: exit routes and buyback

sections.heading: Determine what the operator sells
paragraphs: Vermont Title 9, Chapter 107 concerns defined equipment and machinery dealerships. The dealer and inventory definitions matter even though the agreement may be oral or written. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line dealer category are excluded.

A pure service franchise is not established as covered merely because it uses a trademark. Describe the actual machines, parts, repair work and branded services. Separate activities in the factual file so the reviewer can apply the definitions and exclusions to what the parties really do.

sections.heading: The usual process is not the only process
paragraphs: Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day opportunity to correct the stated problem. It has a separate market-penetration termination process involving an initial 24-month period and a final notice period. Specified events permit immediate termination.

The reason for ending the agreement therefore affects the route to examine. A supplier should retain the actual performance requirements, notice history and reasons, rather than treating 120 days as a universal instruction or assuming an immediate-termination exception applies.

sections.heading: Choose a reason-to-process branch before using a deadline
paragraphs: For the Dutch service-plus-equipment example, classify the equipment relationship first, then the intended exit event, then the requested inventory. Those are three separate decisions.

rows: Is this the defined equipment dealership?
Title 9, Chapter 107 uses product, dealer and inventory definitions; an agreement may be oral or written. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line category are excluded.
Describe actual equipment, parts, repairs and service rights. A trademark or a pure service offer does not establish coverage.
An ordinary termination ground is being considered
Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day opportunity to correct the stated problem.
Retain the actual requirement, reasons, performance evidence and applicable exceptions; this is not a universal exit clock.
The stated problem is market penetration
Section 4072 has a separate process with an initial 24-month period and a final notice period.
Identify and verify that branch’s actual requirements and final-notice conditions rather than borrowing the ordinary process.
An immediate-termination event is claimed
Specified statutory events permit immediate termination.
Match the actual event to the relevant exception; the supplier’s wish to end the agreement does not establish one.
Finance is planning inventory repurchase
Sections 4073–4074 make repurchase subject to request, item eligibility, valuation and payment requirements.
Link the request to item age, source, condition and title. The total stock balance is not a proved buyback entitlement.

sections.heading: Worked example: services plus utility equipment
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch industrial-services brand adds utility-equipment sales and repairs to its Vermont partner offer. Its original service budget did not account for a warehouse of supplier inventory or the consequences of ending an equipment relationship.

The operations manager separates the equipment, repair and service rights and checks whether the defined dealer relationship is present. If a later performance problem arises, the manager records the requirement, evidence and event being considered. A market-penetration issue is not automatically assigned the same procedure as another termination ground.

Finance maintains item records from purchase: age, source, condition and title. If repurchase is later requested, those records allow a review of eligible items and values. The team does not assume that every line in the inventory account will be reimbursed or that every exit uses the same clock. This fictional exercise does not decide coverage or cause.

sections.heading: A buyback claim needs more than a stock total
paragraphs: Sections 4073–4074 address repurchase subject to request, eligibility, valuation and payment requirements. Record what is requested, by whom and when, and link it to the particular items and applicable conditions.

Keeping an inventory ledger and planning possible cash exposure are management methods. They do not establish a legal entitlement or enlarge the items covered. The payment owner should budget an obligation only after identifying the actual statutory branch and evidence.

sections.heading: Keep the equipment relationship file ready
bullets: Identify actual products, dealer status and facts relevant to excluded categories.
Retain written terms or evidence of the oral agreement and reasonable performance requirements.
Record the intended termination event, reasons and selected statutory process.
Keep purchase, condition, title and any repurchase-request records by item.
Assign valuation, return and payment questions, alongside separate franchise/operating-law review.

seoTitle: Virginia franchise exemptions: entity evidence, Form H and delivery

sections.heading: Start with the selected exemption, not the group’s reputation
paragraphs: The SCC says franchises offered or sold in Virginia must be registered or exempt. Its overview identifies potential conditions involving experience, financial condition and the characteristics of the offer or grant, and directs readers to 21VAC5-110-75.

Collect the selling entity’s history and financial statements, group ownership, proposed buyer and transaction structure. Another group company’s operating history cannot simply be substituted where the test concerns the franchisor. Use parent facts only where the selected provision permits them and any required guarantees are established.

sections.heading: The routes differ in conditions and continuing disclosure
paragraphs: The current rule includes routes for unchanged uninterrupted renewal, additional existing-franchisee sales, seasoned franchisors, institutional buyers and substantial investment. Do not choose one merely because its title sounds suitable.

For the routes numbered 3–6, subdivision 7 still requires the disclosure document and all proposed agreements 14 calendar days before agreement or payment. This illustrates why exemption from registration is not a general exemption from delivery to the buyer. Keep the exact authority and conditions for each claimed relief.

sections.heading: Form H and renewal need route-specific dates
paragraphs: The seasoned and substantial-investment routes require their specified Form H package at least ten business days before the covered offer/sale and have annual renewal rules. The institutional route requires its package at least ten business days before each offer or sale of each franchise. Material changes trigger exemption amendment.

The specific annual routes say at least ten business days before expiry, while paragraph 8(c)(1) says ten days. Preserve both wordings and resolve the selected route before relying on the shorter reading. The rule’s electronic-media wording also does not establish the exclusive current submission channel.

sections.heading: Use a route-and-evidence comparison, not the word exempt alone
paragraphs: In the parent-and-new-seller example, the comparison tells the secretary what must be proved and which date belongs to which task. It deliberately does not supply the full eligibility test or choose an exemption for the group.

headers: Facts and dates already established here
rows: Select an exemption under 21VAC5-110-75

Identify the precise provision and the entity or person required to meet each condition. The rule lists renewal, additional-sale, seasoned-franchisor, institutional-buyer and substantial-investment routes.
An experienced parent’s facts count only where the selected provision permits them and any required guarantee is established; a new seller cannot simply borrow group reputation.
Seasoned-franchisor or substantial-investment route
The specified Form H package is required at least ten business days before the covered offer/sale; these routes have annual renewal rules.
The route name or filed form does not prove its financial, history or transaction conditions.
Institutional-buyer route
The specified package is required at least ten business days before each offer or sale of each franchise.
Do not copy the annual-route calendar without checking this transaction-specific filing requirement.
Buyer delivery under routes numbered 3–6
Subdivision 7 retains delivery of the disclosure document and all proposed agreements 14 calendar days before agreement or payment.
Registration relief is not general relief from buyer delivery.
Annual renewal or a material change
The specific annual routes say at least ten business days before expiry; paragraph 8(c)(1) says ten days. Material changes trigger exemption amendment.
Keep both wordings and resolve the selected route before relying on the shorter reading. Electronic-media wording does not establish the exclusive current channel.
The agreement contains governing-law or competition terms
Use the separate Virginia contract guide for the July 2026 changes, negotiated-sale exception and amendment-before-sale instructions.
Neither an exemption memo nor Form H validates the contract terms.

sections.heading: Worked example: an experienced parent and a new seller
paragraphs: Fictional example: a French services group has operated for many years, but a newly formed subsidiary will grant Virginia rights. The expansion director prepares a two-entity chart rather than describing the whole group as one experienced franchisor.

The reviewer identifies the proposed exemption and checks which entity must supply the history, financial evidence or guarantee. The secretary maps any Form H package to the actual first covered offer/sale and records annual and material-change tasks. The sales owner separately schedules disclosure of all proposed agreements where required.
If a condition is unproved, the exemption remains unresolved. The parent’s brand history is evidence to examine, not automatic permission for a different company to sell.

sections.heading: Exemption status does not update the contract automatically
paragraphs: The current Act and SCC’s April notice require separate attention to the July 2026 Virginia governing-law and post-term retail-competition changes, including the negotiated-sale exception. The separate contract guide explains those conditions and the amendment-before-sale instructions.
A group-history memo or registration record does not complete that task. Review the actual FDD, agreement and planned sale dates rather than assuming that a selected exemption validates every term.

sections.heading: Prepare the exemption decision and evidence list
bullets: Name the precise provision and each condition, with the entity/person that must satisfy it.
Attach the relevant history, financial statements, ownership and any permitted parent guarantee evidence.
Retain Form H/other filing acknowledgment or explain the actual self-executing route.
Calendar disclosure, route-specific advance filing, annual renewal and material changes separately.
Assign advertising, ongoing relationship and 2026 contract-language review.

seoTitle: Virginia retail-franchise contracts: July 1, 2026 changes

sections.heading: First establish that the Act covers the arrangement
paragraphs: The current Retail Franchising Act and SCC’s April 14, 2026 notice confirm that chapters 553 and 554 took effect July 1, 2026. Section 13.1-559 requires a written retail marketing-plan/brand arrangement with a direct or indirect franchise fee of $500 or more, subject to its fee exclusions.

The Act applies only where performance contemplates or requires the franchisee to establish or maintain a Virginia place of business. The statute defines that term and contains incidental/ancillary and department exceptions. Incidental or ancillary means secondary to another activity, but the exact statutory exception must still be applied; the description alone is not an exemption.

sections.heading: The two contract provisions answer different questions
paragraphs: Section 13.1-559(D) requires Virginia law for franchise contracts offered or entered into pursuant to the Act. Review the actual governing-law clause, not just the cover sheet.

Section 13.1-563(A)(4) makes it unlawful to offer or enter a franchise agreement restricting the franchisee’s retail offering, selling or distribution of goods/services after termination or expiration. The stated activity and trigger matter. This guide does not decide the validity of confidentiality, intellectual-property or other distinct obligations.

sections.heading: The negotiated-sale exception is specific
paragraphs: Section 563(B) permits the stated restriction where the franchisee sells the franchise at a mutually agreed price to a third party or back to the franchisor, for no more than two years after sale.

Retain the real transaction, price, buyer/seller and restriction period. Ordinary expiry, calling something termination or paying an unrelated invoice does not establish this exception. It should not be presented as a general two-year permission for every post-term restriction.

sections.heading: Compare the clause, exception and sale-document tasks
paragraphs: Chapters 553 and 554 took effect July 1, 2026. The example’s November offer therefore requires a dated coverage-and-document comparison, not an assumption based on when registration began.

rows: Act coverage before clause review

Section 13.1-559 uses the written retail marketing-plan/brand arrangement, a direct or indirect franchise fee of $500 or more subject to fee exclusions, and the defined Virginia place-of-business requirement with stated exceptions.
First establish those facts; neither a service label nor the ordinary meaning of incidental establishes an exception.
Governing-law clause
Section 13.1-559(D) requires Virginia law for franchise contracts offered or entered into pursuant to the Act.
Read the actual clause selecting another state’s law; an earlier registration does not update it.
Post-term retail restriction
Section 13.1-563(A)(4) addresses restrictions on the franchisee’s retail offering, selling or distribution of goods/services after termination or expiration.
The fictional three-year post-expiry restriction needs review within that scope. This does not decide confidentiality, intellectual-property or other distinct obligations.
Negotiated-sale exception
Section 563(B) permits the stated restriction following a sale to a third party or back to the franchisor at a mutually agreed price, for no more than two years after sale.
Ordinary expiry and an unrelated payment do not establish this sale exception; it is not general two-year permission.
FDD/agreement versions and amendment

The SCC’s April 14, 2026 notice calls for the new language in the documents, through relevant Item 17 disclosure or a Virginia addendum. For pre-July registrations expiring later, it distinguishes no expected Virginia sale before expiry from a possible or actual sale on or after July 1; the latter requires an amendment application first.
Record the applicable sale branch and amendment evidence before continuing the covered sale process. This does not determine old signed agreements’ enforceability or a cause/remedy dispute.

sections.heading: Worked example: a November offer with a pre-July template
paragraphs: Fictional example: a French services group plans a November 2026 Virginia offer under a registration that began before July. Its template selects another state’s law and contains a three-year post-expiry retail restriction.

The secretary first checks the Act’s actual coverage, then compares the FDD and agreement with the enacted changes. The SCC notice calls for the new language in those documents, using relevant Item 17 disclosure or a Virginia addendum. For offerings registered before July 1 with later expiry, the notice distinguishes no expected Virginia sale before expiry from a possible or actual sale on or after July 1. The latter requires an amendment application first. The secretary records the applicable branch, amendment and actual document version before continuing the covered sale process.

paragraphs: Section 13.1-564 separately restricts cancellation without reasonable cause and undue influence to surrender franchise rights. sections.heading: Begin with the actual relationship and offer facts
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral, written and implied arrangements, a marketing plan prescribed or suggested in substantial part, substantial brand association and the defined franchise fee. Required goods/services and training charges can matter; bona fide wholesale, property and other specified payments have exclusions.

The state definition also has independent insurance and motor-vehicle exclusions. A licence label or federal classification does not replace this test. Under 19.100.020, registration or exemption review belongs before the covered offer, not only before collecting money. Future outlet location alone does not establish all state connections, and separate business-opportunity law is not exhausted here.

sections.heading: Give each event its own calendar entry
paragraphs: The reviewed rules have different clocks. Initial disclosure under RCW 19.100.080 uses 14 calendar days. A specified unilateral material agreement change uses seven calendar days, with prospect-initiated negotiations treated separately. Keep the revised text and negotiation record so the appropriate branch can be checked.

For covered advertising, a true copy must be filed at least seven days before publication unless a shorter period is allowed. The submitted version, planned channel and intended-use date should match the material actually scheduled. Completing one document task does not automatically complete the others.

sections.heading: Annual renewal does not absorb intervening changes
paragraphs: Under 19.100.070, the ordinary registration and identified exemption-claim period is one year from effectiveness/filing unless the director sets another period. A registration renewal application is due no later than 20 calendar days before expiry.

A material adverse condition change or material disclosure change must be amended as soon as reasonably possible and before another franchise sale. Keep the event date, amendment, delivered version and next sale connected. Waiting for annual renewal is not the stated material-change procedure.

sections.heading: Keep the event and the source’s day unit together
paragraphs: In the national-account example, a changed territory promise can affect the agreement, what the prospect was told and the advertisement. Each mismatch needs its own version record and applicable review; one completed filing does not settle the others.

seoTitle: Washington franchise termination vs nonrenewal: cause and compensation

sections.heading: Establish this state relationship before using its protections
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral/written and express/implied arrangements involving the stated substantially prescribed or suggested marketing plan, brand association and franchise fee. Required purchases and training can matter, while the fee definition contains wholesale, property and other specific exceptions. Insurance and specified motor-vehicle relationships receive separate treatment.
Neither federal classification nor the word licence decides this state test. Describe the actual agreement, payments and relevant Washington connections before applying the relationship provisions.

sections.heading: What is the promised territory?
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(f) addresses franchisor competition and competitive grants where the agreement provides an exclusive territory, which must be specified in the agreement. It does not create exclusivity for every franchise.

Map the territory, national-account reservations, online leads and service duties before promising protection. Approved-source purchasing and conduct standards have their own reasonableness/business-ground tests; exclusivity language does not answer those separate issues.

sections.heading: Termination requires the right cause and correction analysis
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(j) restricts termination before expiry to good cause. Its ordinary default branch uses written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure that need not exceed 30 days. That is not an unconditional 30-day minimum or an automatic right to terminate on day 31. Where the problem cannot reasonably be cured within 30 days, the text separately addresses substantial and continuing corrective action initiated within that time.

The repeated-breach branch requires three willful and material breaches of the same term within 12 months, with the specified prior notices/opportunities, before the exception for a subsequent willful and material breach of that same term within the same 12 months. A list of unrelated complaints does not establish those conditions.

Adjudicated bankruptcy/insolvency, assignment for creditors, voluntary abandonment and the specified business-related criminal outcome have separate immediate-action conditions. Alleging one of these events is not proof that its requirements are met.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal has a different compensation question
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(i) addresses fair compensation at expiry for listed assets bought from the franchisor and goodwill, with exclusions and offsets. The goodwill exception requires both one year’s nonrenewal notice and written agreement not to enforce a covenant restraining competition. One condition alone is insufficient, and this exception does not erase every listed asset obligation.

Termination for good cause has its own narrower inventory/supplies purchase rule, including a premises-retention qualification. Keep these ledgers separate rather than assuming that the less costly result can be chosen by changing the action’s label.

sections.heading: Classify the action before selecting a process or ledger
paragraphs: For the replacement-operator example, first ask whether the company proposes early termination, nonrenewal or a competitive change. Then match evidence and money records to that event; exclusive-territory promises remain a separate question.

This has its own narrower purchase rule, including a premises-retention qualification.

paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch facilities brand wants to replace a Washington operator after missed response targets, while retaining a national customer inside the promised territory. The reviewer identifies whether the proposed event is early termination, nonrenewal or a competitive change.

The team then applies the appropriate cause/cure conditions and the exact territorial promise. Finance makes separate records for expiry compensation and any good-cause termination inventory/supplies question. The manager cannot select the cheaper ledger by calling every exit a termination. This example organises the decision without deciding cause, compensation or enforceability.

seoTitle: West Virginia equipment dealers: notice and inventory repurchase

sections.heading: The title does not limit the inquiry to farm machines
paragraphs: The Farm Equipment Dealer Contract Act includes specified retail sellers of construction, industrial and outdoor power equipment, with inventory and repair-service conditions. Those conditions are part of coverage, not optional background facts.

The supplier and operator should record what is sold at retail, which inventory obligations exist and who provides repairs. A brand licence or service contract alone does not establish that the Act applies. Conversely, a business should not ignore the Act simply because its equipment is industrial rather than agricultural.

sections.heading: Notice is a procedure, not only a period
paragraphs: Section 47-11F-3 generally requires six months’ termination notice, prescribed written service and stated contents. Listed exceptions and a mutual-consent route need separate examination. Keep the reason, method, contents and effective date together.

Do not casually replace six months with an assumed number of days or treat an informal message as proof of prescribed service. Nor does the existence of a contract clause settle whether the relevant statutory branch and exception have been followed. This guide does not choose a termination route for any actual relationship.

sections.heading: Map coverage, notice and repurchase to different records
paragraphs: The example’s machine sales and repairs may raise a different question from its service-brand rights. This map keeps that coverage inquiry ahead of notice or buyback assumptions.

rows: Section 47-11F-2: is this the defined dealer?
The reviewed Act includes specified retail sellers of construction, industrial and outdoor power equipment, with inventory and repair-service conditions.
Separate actual retail products, inventory commitments and repair roles from branded maintenance services; neither the farm-equipment title nor a service label decides coverage.
Section 47-11F-3: how would termination be notified?
The general rule is six months’ notice, with prescribed written service and contents. Listed exceptions and a mutual-consent route need separate review.
Keep reason, method, contents and effective date together. Do not convert six months into an assumed day count or treat an informal message as prescribed service.
Sections 47-11F-4–5: what inventory qualifies and at what value?
Repurchase is conditional, with valuation, timing and exclusions. A gross stock balance does not establish eligibility or value.
Keep item source, age, condition, title and relevant current-net-price evidence rather than assuming retail price or the accounting balance applies.
Sections 47-11F-4–5: what has been returned and paid?
Termination, physical return and payment are separate events to track under the applicable conditions.
Link return records to the responsible payer and unresolved warranty questions; a budget for possible exposure is not a proved entitlement.

sections.heading: Worked example: equipment sales alongside a maintenance service
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European maintenance brand appoints a West Virginia partner to sell machines and provide repairs. The commercial plan describes the whole arrangement as a service partnership, but the operator also has equipment inventory commitments.

The operations manager separates retail sales, repair services and branded customer work. The reviewer uses those facts to test dealer coverage. Finance builds item records with purchase source, age, condition, ownership and pricing evidence before a possible exit.

If the supplier later proposes termination, the secretary identifies the actual event and examines the notice method, contents, date and any claimed exception or mutual-consent route. The contract and the operational records are read together. The example illustrates preparation; it does not establish that either party qualifies or that termination is lawful.

sections.heading: Inventory value and payment are different questions
paragraphs: Sections 4–5 govern conditional inventory repurchase, including valuation, timing and exclusions. A gross stock balance cannot show what qualifies, whether an item is excluded or how its value must be measured.

Track the termination date, physical return and payment separately. Finance should retain the relevant current-net-price evidence and any return information, then identify the responsible payer and unresolved warranty issues. A company can budget possible exposure while leaving disputed eligibility or amounts open; the budget itself is not a legal entitlement.

Keep item-level age, condition, source, title, pricing and exclusion evidence.
Assign repurchase return/payment responsibilities and remaining warranty questions separately.

seoTitle: Wisconsin franchise registration: receipt, disclosure and amendments

sections.heading: Registration and buyer delivery have different starting events
paragraphs: DFI says a franchise must be registered no later than its first Wisconsin franchise sale. Registration is described as effective on receipt, and the agency expressly says Wisconsin is not a franchise merit-review state. A buyer should not treat the receipt as validation of projections, management or the model.

The agency separately requires an FDD 14 calendar days before the earlier signing of a binding franchise or other agreement, or payment. Filing on receipt does not start or replace that buyer-delivery clock. Keep the recipient, document version and actual delivery date.

sections.heading: Each system and each event needs the correct filing record
paragraphs: DFI lists a $400 registration fee and one-year effectiveness, and says each franchise system needs a separate filing. A group should identify whether it is selling different systems instead of assuming one corporate name means one filing.

The agency lists material-event amendments within 30 days, with a $200 fee. An amendment does not restart the registration year. These amounts were checked against the agency FAQ on the recorded review date and should be rechecked before payment. A diary entry for next year’s renewal cannot replace reviewing a material event now.

sections.heading: Keep a separate event row for each franchise system
paragraphs: The existing DFI franchise FAQ and filing instructions answer sales-filing and delivery questions. The Fair Dealership Law sources answer a different operating-relationship question; the records should show that distinction.

Later, the group reorganises its corporate structure. Rather than waiting automatically for annual renewal, the secretary sends the actual change for assessment as a possible material event. If an amendment is required, its timing and fee are recorded without replacing the existing registration-year dates.

The sales manager separately checks that each prospective buyer’s 14-calendar-day period has run before the earlier covered agreement or payment. A same-day registration receipt cannot show that the buyer received the right documents two weeks earlier. The example demonstrates event control, not approval of a particular filing or reorganisation.

sections.heading: The operating relationship has its own legal test
paragraphs: The agency FAQ also points to Wisconsin’s Fair Dealership Law. Chapter 135’s dealership/community-of-interest inquiry is independent of sales registration. A registration receipt or federal franchise-fee analysis does not decide whether that operating law applies.

The separate dealership guide addresses in-state scope, exclusions, good cause, notice/cure and marked inventory. In particular, the nonpayment branch does not turn a ten-day cure notice into an automatic day-11 termination right. Keep relationship changes and exits assigned even where registration is straightforward.

Review important events for the 30-day amendment task; do not restart the year because an amendment is filed.
Recheck the current fee before payment.

seoTitle: Wisconsin Fair Dealership Law: notice versus cure on exit

sections.heading: Use the operating-law definition
paragraphs: Chapter 135 can include express or implied, oral or written agreements granting sale/distribution rights or use of a commercial symbol, with a community of interest. A federal fee analysis or Wisconsin registration does not establish that separate test.

Section 135.07 excludes the specified motor-vehicle dealer/distributor/wholesaler acting in that capacity, insurance business and door-to-door marketing of goods or services. Liquor has its own provisions. Record how the business actually sells and operates rather than assuming a trademark either creates protection or establishes an exclusion.

sections.heading: Justification and notice both need evidence
paragraphs: Section 135.03 prohibits covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes without good cause, placing the burden of establishing cause on the grantor. Calling conduct a default does not establish that cause exists.

Section 135.04 ordinarily requires 90 days’ prior written notice stating all reasons and 60 days to rectify the claimed deficiency. Timely correction voids the notice. Insolvency, assignment for creditors and bankruptcy have stated notice exceptions; examine the actual branch rather than extending the ordinary rule to every event.

sections.heading: For nonpayment, distinguish ten days to fix from the advance notice
paragraphs: The statute supplies written nonpayment-default notice and ten days to remedy from delivery or posting. The cited official civil jury instruction’s comment expressly preserves 90 days’ advance notice for this branch while shortening cure to ten days.

The two clocks answer different questions. One concerns the opportunity to fix the payment problem; the other concerns advance notice of the proposed action. A ten-day demand should therefore not be scheduled as automatic authority to terminate on day 11. The older instruction is used for this specific explanation alongside the current certified statute.

sections.heading: Put advance notice and correction on different tracks
paragraphs: For the unpaid-invoice example, day 11 alone proves neither cause nor completion of advance notice. First establish the in-state dealership/community-of-interest test and exclusions. No independent full appellate opinion was reviewed; the older instruction has only the limited explanatory role stated here.

rows: Ordinary covered action: current certified Chapter 135, sections 135.03–.04

Good cause is required for the stated termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes, with the grantor bearing that burden. The ordinary written notice is 90 days and must state all reasons.
The ordinary period to rectify the claimed deficiency is 60 days; timely correction voids the notice. Cause, advance notice and cure are separate requirements.
Nonpayment: current statute read with the older official civil jury instruction’s specific comment
The instruction preserves 90 days’ advance notice for this branch; it is not being presented as a newly reviewed appellate judgment.
Written nonpayment-default notice gives ten days to remedy from delivery or posting. That shorter correction period does not establish automatic day-11 termination.
Specified insolvency, assignment or bankruptcy event
The statute has stated notice exceptions; establish the actual event and applicable branch.
Do not use the ordinary track or a claimed exception without its conditions.
Grantor-initiated termination and inventory: section 135.045
At the dealer’s option, conditional repurchase concerns qualifying inventory sold by the grantor for resale at fair wholesale market value.
The merchandise must bear an identifying grantor mark. Separate that resale stock from a computer or service tool used to run the business.

sections.heading: Worked example: unpaid invoices and a nearby replacement
paragraphs: Fictional example: a British grounds-care supplier plans to end a Wisconsin dealer after unpaid invoices and appoint a nearby seller. The manager first tests dealership/community-of-interest coverage and exclusions. The proposed competitive change is recorded as well as the proposed termination.

The team preserves the cause evidence, default wording and delivery/posting record, then separately calendars the applicable advance notice and correction requirements. Finance identifies grantor-marked resale stock separately from service tools. A supplier cannot assume that selecting the shortest apparent deadline completes the other conditions. This example does not decide cause or authorise the action.

sections.heading: Inventory and remedies have their own conditions
paragraphs: Under section 135.045, grantor-initiated termination can trigger, at the dealer’s option, repurchase at fair wholesale market value of qualifying inventory sold by the grantor for resale. The section is confined to merchandise bearing an identifying grantor mark. A computer or service tool does not qualify merely because it helped run the business.
Section 135.06 provides a conditional damages, costs/fees and injunction route. A checklist does not establish injury, an award or a successful court application.

sections.heading: Prepare the action file
bullets: Keep in-state dealership facts, agreement rights, community-of-interest evidence and exclusion analysis.
Identify the actual proposed action and cause evidence.
Retain all reasons, notice delivery/posting, separate clocks and correction records.
Identify grantor-supplied marked resale inventory and valuation evidence.
Assign remedy, arbitration, federal and specialised industry questions separately.

seoTitle: Wyoming equipment dealers: general vs single-line notice and cure

sections.heading: Separate the equipment arrangement from customer services
paragraphs: Title 40, Chapter 20 addresses defined equipment dealers and suppliers. Its product scope includes specified industrial, maintenance, utility and grounds-care equipment. Dealer status, single-line status, exclusions and the actual agreement must be checked before using these protections.

Describe machines, parts, repair rights and the customer services separately. Owning equipment or using a brand does not automatically answer the supplier/dealer test. This factual separation also helps the company see which stock and required tools create possible exit exposure.

sections.heading: The two ordinary notice regimes are different
paragraphs: The general sections 115/117 regime ordinarily uses 180 days’ notice with 60 days to cure. The single-line section 116 regime ordinarily uses 90 days with 60 days to cure. First establish the actual branch; do not choose whichever period fits the preferred commercial schedule.

Specified events and performance failures have different conditions. Preserve the reason for action, comparable performance standards, relevant notices and improvement history. These are conditional industry rules, not a general right to end any franchise simply by waiting out a notice period.

sections.heading: Establish the dealer category before choosing either ordinary track
paragraphs: In the grounds-care example, the factual sequence is equipment relationship, dealer category, intended action and reason, then the applicable process. The commercial schedule cannot supply a missing legal fact.

headers: What the reader must not assume

Check Chapter 40-20’s products, dealer/supplier roles, agreement, exclusions and actual single-line conditions. Separate equipment rights from customer services.
Owning machines, using one brand or preferring a shorter timetable does not prove the relevant category.
General sections 40-20-115/117 regime
Ordinarily 180 days’ notice with 60 days to cure.
The figures do not remove the stated event, performance or exception conditions or create automatic permission to exit.
Single-line section 40-20-116 regime
Ordinarily 90 days’ notice with 60 days to cure.
Single-line status must be established; this is not an alternative the supplier can choose for convenience.
Performance failure or specified event
Different conditions apply; retain the actual reason, comparable standards, prior notices and improvement history.
Neither ordinary row is a complete answer for every event.
Inventory or succession question
Sections 120–121 and the separate inventory guide concern conditional repurchase; an actual succession request needs separate facts and review.
The notice figure does not establish buyback of every startup cost or decide succession.

sections.heading: Worked example: grounds-care sales plus service contracts
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas brand supplies machines, parts and repair know-how to a Wyoming operator that also sells grounds-care services to local customers. The team’s first draft treats the entire relationship as a single service licence.

The operations manager separates equipment dealership rights from the operator’s customer-service contracts. The reviewer tests the actual products, dealer/supplier status, exclusions and any single-line conditions. If the supplier later proposes termination, the file identifies the actual action and reason before selecting the general or single-line notice branch.

Finance has already retained inventory and required-tool records. That allows a later repurchase review without assuming that the supplier must repay every startup cost. Any succession request is recorded with its actual facts rather than being treated as resolved by the termination calendar.
The example illustrates why the agreement and operational evidence need to be read together. It does not decide that the operator is protected, establish a performance default or authorise an exit.

sections.heading: Repurchase does not follow automatically from the notice figure
paragraphs: Sections 120–121 contain repurchase duties and exclusions. Coverage of the relationship does not establish eligibility of every item. Record the property, source, dates, condition, return events and payment questions separately from the cause and notice decision.

The separate Wyoming inventory guide explains the detailed evidence categories. A financial estimate can help management plan, but it should show assumptions and unresolved items instead of treating the accounting stock balance as a guaranteed recovery.

bullets: Attach product, dealer and supplier definitions and exclusion facts.
Document why the general or single-line branch is relevant.
Record the action, reason, performance standards and any specific exception.
Keep notice, correction and performance-improvement history in date order.
Identify inventory eligibility, returns, payment duties and any succession request for separate review.

seoTitle: Wyoming equipment buyback: valuation, returns and payment evidence

sections.heading: Confirm the relationship and separate the item categories
paragraphs: Chapter 40-20 defines the relevant dealer, supplier, equipment and agreement. Dealer status combines selling/leasing to consumers and repair/service activities with stated exclusions. Mere ownership of a machine is insufficient. Closing a covered location can also raise inventory issues under the agreement definition.

This page concerns repurchase evidence. The separate Wyoming hub addresses good-cause and notice branches. A decision that an item may qualify for buyback does not answer whether the relationship was lawfully ended.

sections.heading: Use the legal price basis, not one percentage for everything
paragraphs: Section 120 distinguishes new eligible equipment, qualifying demonstrators and repair parts. Its ordinary figures include 100% of net equipment cost and 95% of current net parts prices for qualifying items, with separate handling/freight and demonstrator conditions.

Required data-processing hardware/software uses the stated three-year straight-line acquisition-cost approach, with a minimum-specification qualification. Specialised repair tools have a 75% invoice rule. Keep supplier-requirement and actual-cost evidence. An ordinary computer or tool is not automatically eligible because the dealer used it.

sections.heading: Eligibility depends on source, condition and dates
paragraphs: Section 121 addresses damaged packages, parts needing reconditioning, clear title, retained goods, condition, equipment delivered before the stated 36-month window, post-notice orders and goods from other sources. Apply the actual qualifications and exceptions: a broken package does not always mean zero recovery.

The return provision in 121(a)(ix) is tied to the later of effective termination and receipt of required return-policy information, with its stated notice qualification. It is not simply 90 days from any letter. Retain the information, when it arrived and what the notice said before treating a return as late.

sections.heading: Separate valuation rows from return and cash events
paragraphs: Use one item row for eligibility and valuation, then separate event rows for return, supplier receipt and settlement. The fictional $11,900 can be arithmetically correct while return facts, offsets or collection remain unresolved.

rows: Eligible new equipment and qualifying demonstrators
Section 120 distinguishes these categories; the ordinary equipment figure is 100% of net equipment cost, with separate demonstrator, handling and freight conditions.
Keep the defined cost, condition and eligibility evidence; book value or retail price is not automatically the legal basis.
Qualifying repair parts
The ordinary figure is 95% of current net parts prices, subject to the actual qualifications.
Retain current price, source, condition and exclusion evidence; a damaged package is not automatically zero recovery under every qualification.
Required data-processing hardware/software
The stated three-year straight-line acquisition-cost approach has a minimum-specification qualification.
Prove the supplier requirement, specification and acquisition cost. Do not apply the equipment or parts percentage to an ordinary computer.
Specialised repair tools
The stated rule is 75% of invoice, subject to eligibility.
Keep invoice and supplier-requirement evidence; business use alone does not establish eligibility.
Fictional proved equipment and parts inputs
$10,000 × 100% + $2,000 × 95% = $11,900 before separate handling, freight, offsets and other applicable conditions.
The example supplies no technology or tool amounts and is not a valuation, approved claim or collection forecast.
Return timing under section 121(a)(ix)
The stated trigger is tied to the later of effective termination and receipt of required return-policy information, with its notice qualification.
Record both events and what the notice said. It is not simply 90 days from any letter. Apply item age, title, source, retention and other exclusions separately.
Payment or credit under section 120(b)
Generally within 90 days after the supplier receives covered property, with the stated signage-removal withholding condition.
Keep actual supplier receipt and signage evidence. Requests, shipping and receivables do not prove receipt or payment; outstanding sums can produce account credit rather than cash.

sections.heading: Worked example: calculate only the proved eligible items
paragraphs: Fictional example: assume a covered dealer establishes $10,000 of eligible net equipment cost and $2,000 of eligible current net parts prices. The basic calculation is $10,000 × 100% plus $2,000 × 95%, producing $11,900 before separate handling, freight, offsets and other applicable conditions.

sections.heading: Payment runs from another event
paragraphs: Section 120(b) generally requires payment or credit within 90 days after the supplier receives covered property. It permits withholding during failure to satisfy the stated contractual signage-removal obligation. Outstanding sums may produce account credit rather than cash.

Keep supplier receipt, offsets, signage and shared freight evidence with the amount calculation. Sending a request, shipping stock or recording a receivable does not prove supplier receipt or payment.

sections.heading: Prepare the return-and-receipt ledger
bullets: Separate machines, demonstrators, parts, required technology and specialised tools.
Attach invoices, statutory price bases, title, condition, age and current parts evidence.
Retain supplier-required specifications and cost records for technology/tools.
Track effective termination, return-policy information, notice qualification, shipping and actual receipt.
Reconcile debt credits, handling/freight and signage obligations separately from expected cash.
Keep termination/cure, buyback and dispute-remedy questions independently assigned.
